I am checking p2's holdings to verify whether they already own Virginia with three houses before the trade. The log shows St Charles at two houses and States at three, but I need to confirm if Virginia was already fully developed.

p2 currently owns St Charles with two houses, States with three, and Virginia with three. That totals eight houses, matching the build action. I am checking whether they started from zero after the trade or already had those houses.

The holdings snapshot appears to reflect the current game state. p2 built eight houses this turn, but the distribution is uneven: St Charles has two, States has three, and Virginia has three. That violates standard Monopoly rules requiring even building, though I will trust the game state as-is. Virginia with three houses charges $500 in rent, matching States at the same level.

St Charles with two houses charges $180 in rent. p1 owns New York Avenue with three houses at $650, Tennessee Avenue with two at $220, and St James Avenue with two at $220. Kentucky and Indiana are mortgaged, so p1 may not have a complete orange monopoly. Still, they have houses on all three orange properties.

Existing houses remain valid even when other properties in the same group are mortgaged, so p1's three houses on New York Avenue still charge $650. If they pay $50 to get out of jail, my cash would drop to $239 after paying that rent.

Bidding $79 would leave me with $810, which is enough to survive both New York Avenue and Virginia Avenue. The mortgage arbitrage value of $140 is less appealing because I already have $889 in cash.

The mortgage arbitrage is not worthwhile because the purchase price would be nearly $140. The real value of owning Marvin Gardens is the option to complete a yellow monopoly later.

p4 owns Ventnor, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania. They have only $29 cash and hotels on Mediterranean and Baltic. They could go bankrupt if they hit a high rent.

A completed yellow monopoly would be extremely strong, with three houses on each property charging roughly $800 to $850. Only p4 and I can benefit from winning Marvin Gardens, since p1 and p2 have no yellows and p4 is already out of the auction. p1 is bidding up from $76 to $78 in a slow, incremental way that seems designed to exhaust my cash. They likely want the property only as a mortgage chip or trade token.

p1 can mortgage Marvin Gardens for $140 after buying it, netting roughly $60 in cash. That makes a bid of about $139 the maximum they would pay purely for arbitrage. I should be willing to bid higher than that because the property also gives me the strategic option of completing a yellow monopoly.

A trade for Ventnor is unlikely. p4 wants Pacific Avenue to complete a green monopoly, but I own only Pacific and lack the other greens. Completing the green set would cost me roughly $1,700 in rent. The yellow option value is therefore limited.

I will bid $79 and continue the slow incremental war. I am not giving Pacific Avenue to p4, so completing a yellow monopoly requires p4 to go bankrupt or trade without finishing their green set. I will hold Marvin as a waiting position. I should not show a ceiling.

At $180 I would have $709 left, which barely survives New York Avenue at $650 but still covers Virginia Avenue at $500. At $160 I would have $729, leaving only $79 after New York Avenue. That is too tight.

At $140 I would have $749 left, surviving New York Avenue with a $99 cushion. At $100 I would have $789, leaving $139 after that rent. The dark blue build plan requires a larger buffer first. One house on Boardwalk costs $200 and raises rent to $200. One house on Park Place costs $175 and raises rent to $175.

Building one house on each dark blue property would cost $400 and leave only $489. That is too little to survive a $500 Virginia Avenue hit or a $650 New York Avenue hit. I will not build yet. I am now considering dropping out of the auction entirely so p1 wastes their $320 cash in jail.

I will bid $79 and keep raising by one dollar increments. I am reconsidering dropping out earlier because a $160 bid leaves only $79 after New York Avenue, which is too tight. I am recalculating the exact cash buffer needed to survive that rent.

Bidding $160 leaves only $79 after New York Avenue, which is too tight to build on. The yellow option is speculative, but paying $20 above mortgage value for it may be worthwhile if the option is real. p4 owns North Carolina, so they do not pay rent to themselves.

p4 is on North Carolina and will likely land on Park Place or Boardwalk next. Both are owned by me, and the rent is unaffordable with only $29 cash. The Luxury Tax of $75 is also beyond their means. They may need to mortgage properties or declare bankruptcy.

p4 cannot pay the doubled Boardwalk rent of $100 with only $29 cash. If they declare bankruptcy to me, I would inherit their entire holdings including Ventnor. That makes owning Marvin Gardens before their bust a strong strategic move. I should not drop out of the auction.

A bankruptcy win would give me a yellow, green, and utility monopoly. I might not be the creditor if p1 or p2 is owed instead. Even without that, owning Marvin makes it a strong trade asset.
